title: Seller Performance Standing Metric Definitions and Measurement Windows
content:
The Seller Performance Standing program measures four metrics for every seller ahead of each monthly evaluation: the order defect rate, the late shipment rate, the seller cancellation rate and the valid tracking rate. Each is taken over a rolling window of calendar days ending the day before the evaluation date. The windows and the counting definitions below are identical at every level — Below Standard Level, Developing Seller Level, Standard Level, Above Standard Level, Top Rated Level and Preferred Partner Level.

## Windows

| Metric | Rolling window (calendar days, ending the day before evaluation) |
|---|---|
| Order defect rate | 60 |
| Late shipment rate | 30 |
| Seller cancellation rate | 30 |
| Valid tracking rate | 30 |

## Definitions

1. **Orders measured.** The rates are computed over the orders of the seller with an order date in the window.
2. **Order defect rate.** Distinct orders of the seller with an order date in the 60-day window that carry at least one recorded defect of a counted type not cancelled by a defect removal, divided by all such orders. When the orders number fewer than the low-volume order threshold, the count of those defective orders is used instead of the rate.
3. **Defect types counted.** Negative feedback, guarantee claim and chargeback make an order defective.
4. **One defective order however many defects.** Several defects on one order count as one defective order in the defect rate.
5. **Guarantee claims funded by Northloop.** A guarantee claim funded by Northloop is excluded from defects (setting: yes).
6. **Chargeback won by the seller.** A chargeback defect is removed when the seller wins the chargeback dispute (setting: yes).
7. **Product reviews.** Product reviews do not count as order defects (setting: product reviews affect standing — no).
8. **Late shipment rate.** Seller-shipped orders of the seller in the window shipped late, divided by seller-shipped orders of the seller in the window. A seller-shipped order counts as shipped late when its shipped date is after the order date plus the maximum handling business days.
9. **Seller cancellation rate.** Orders of the seller in the window cancelled with the seller as the initiator, divided by all orders of the seller in the window. A cancellation for the reason "buyer requested cancellation" does not count toward the cancellation rate.
10. **Valid tracking rate.** Seller-shipped orders of the seller in the window with valid tracking, divided by seller-shipped orders shipped in the window. Tracking counts as valid when there is a carrier scan within one business day of upload.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures)

A seller has 500 orders dated in the 60-day defect window. Twelve of them carry a defect: one order carries both negative feedback and a chargeback, and the other eleven carry one defect each. A further order carries a chargeback the seller later won, so that defect was removed. The defective orders number 12 (the order with two defects counts once; the order whose only defect was removed does not count), and the order defect rate is 12 divided by 500, or 0.024. Because 500 is not below the low-volume threshold, the rate, not the count, is compared with the level's limit.
